title.zh: 卷三十六 列傳第三十 孔休源 江革
title.raw: 卷三十六 列傳第三十 孔休源 江革 Volume 36: Kong Xiuyuan; Jiang Ge

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第三十六 列傳第三十

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 36, Biography 30
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 36, Biography 30

sentences.zh: 孔休源 江革

translations.literal: Kong Xiuyuan; Jiang Ge
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xiuyuan; Jiang Ge

sentences.zh: 孔休源，字慶緒，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Xiuyuan, styled Qingxu, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xiuyuan, styled Qingxu, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 晉丹陽太守沖之八世孫。

translations.literal: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Chongzhi, Administrator of Danyang under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was an eighth-generation descendant of Jin's Danyang administrator Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖遙之，宋尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yaozhi was Water Section Director in the Song Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yaozhi had been Water Section Director under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父珮，齊廬陵王記室參軍，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Pei was Secretary to Prince of Luling of Qi and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pei, a secretary in the household of Qi's Prince of Luling, died young.

sentences.zh: 休源年十一而孤，居喪盡禮，每見父手所寫書，必哀慟流涕，不能自勝，見者莫不爲之垂泣。

translations.literal: At eleven Xiuyuan was orphaned; he observed mourning with full propriety. Whenever he saw books written in his father's own hand, he always wept in grief beyond restraint—and those who saw it never failed to shed tears for him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at eleven, he mourned his father with scrupulous ritual. Books in his father's hand always moved him to uncontrollable tears, and even onlookers wept.

sentences.zh: 後就吳興沈驎士受經，略通大義。

translations.literal: Later he studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a rough grasp of the essential principles.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under Wuxing's Shen Linshi and mastered the classics in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，州舉秀才，太尉徐孝嗣省其策，深善之，謂同坐曰：「董仲舒、華令思何以尚此，可謂後生之准也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu the province recommended him as xiucai; Grand Marshal Xu Xiaosi reviewed his examination answers and deeply approved, saying to those seated with him: "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He may be called the measure of the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year 4 the province nominated him as xiucai. Grand Marshal Xu Xiaosi read his examination paper and praised it to his companions: "Not even Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi would outshine this youth—he is the standard for his generation.

sentences.zh: 觀其此對，足稱王佐之才。

translations.literal: Judging from this response, he is fully worthy to be called talent fit to assist a king.
translations.idiomatic: From this answer alone, he clearly has the makings of a king's right-hand man.

sentences.zh: 」琅邪王融雅相友善，乃薦之於司徒竟陵王，爲西邸學士。

translations.literal: " Wang Rong of Langya was on friendly terms with him and recommended him to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling, where he became a scholar of the Western Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Rong of Langya, who knew him well, recommended him to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling, and he entered the Western Pavilion as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，與南陽劉之遴同爲太學博士，當時以爲美選。

translations.literal: When the Liang platform was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang both became Masters of the Imperial Academy—a choice then regarded as fine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was founded, he and Nanyang's Liu Zhilin were both appointed Masters of the Imperial Academy—an appointment everyone envied.

sentences.zh: 休源初到京，寓於宗人少府卿孔登宅，曾以祠事入廟，侍中范雲一與相遇，深加褒賞，曰：「不期忽覯清顏，頓袪鄙吝，觀天披霧，驗之今日。

translations.literal: When Xiuyuan first arrived in the capital he lodged at the home of his clansman Kong Deng, Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury. Once, entering a temple on sacrificial business, he met Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, who greatly praised him: "To meet your refined countenance unexpectedly dispels my baseness; parting clouds to see the heavens—verified today.
translations.idiomatic: On first reaching the capital he stayed with his kinsman Kong Deng, Junior Director of the Treasury. During a temple visit for sacrifice he met Attendant Fan Yun, who exclaimed: "I never expected to see such a clear face—it sweeps away my vulgarity, like clouds parting to reveal the sky.

sentences.zh: 」後雲命駕到少府門，登便拂筵整帶，謂當詣己，旣而獨造休源，高談盡日，同載還家，登深以爲愧。

translations.literal: " Later Yun ordered his carriage to the Junior Director's gate; Deng hastened to arrange the feast and straighten his sash, expecting Yun had come for him—but Yun went alone to Xiuyuan, talked at length all day, and returned home sharing the same carriage; Deng was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Yun drove to the Junior Director's gate. Deng hurried to set out cushions and straighten his sash, sure the visit was for him. Instead Yun sought out Xiuyuan alone, talked all day, and rode home with him—leaving Deng deeply mortified.

sentences.zh: 尚書令沈約當朝貴顯，軒蓋盈門，休源或時後來，必虛襟引接，處之坐右，商略文義。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Shen Yue held great influence at court, his gateway always crowded with visitors; whenever Xiuyuan arrived late, Yue would always receive him with an open mind, seat him at his right hand, and discuss literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Shen Yue, then at the height of power with a constant throng at his gate, always made room for Xiuyuan when he came late, seated him on the right, and debated texts with him.

sentences.zh: 其爲通人所推如此。

translations.literal: In this way he was esteemed by those of broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard in which men of culture held him.

sentences.zh: 俄除臨川王府行參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Adjunct in the Princely Household of Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made an adjutant in Prince of Linchuan's household.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗問吏部尚書徐勉曰：「今帝業初基，須一人有學藝解朝儀者，爲尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked Minister of Personnel Xu Mian: "Now that imperial enterprise is newly founded, we need someone learned in the arts who understands court rites to serve as Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once asked Xu Mian, Minister of Personnel: "The dynasty is just taking shape. I need a learned man who knows court ceremony for Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 爲朕思之，誰堪其選？

translations.literal: Think for me—who is fit for this choice?"
translations.idiomatic: Think for me—who can fill the post?"

sentences.zh: 」勉對曰：「孔休源識具清通，諳練故實，自晉、宋《起居注》誦略上口。

translations.literal: Mian replied: "Kong Xiuyuan has clear, thorough knowledge and is versed in antiquity; the Jin and Song Daily Records he can recite from memory nearly word for word.
translations.idiomatic: Mian answered: "Kong Xiuyuan is lucid, well grounded in precedent, and can recite the Jin and Song Daily Records almost by heart.

sentences.zh: 」高祖亦素聞之，卽日除兼尚書儀曹郎中。

translations.literal: " The Emperor too had long heard of him and the same day appointed him Acting Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu had already heard of him and appointed him Acting Director of Ritual that very day.

sentences.zh: 是時多所改作，每逮訪前事，休源卽以所誦記隨機斷決，曾無疑滯。

translations.literal: At that time many reforms were underway; whenever they consulted him on past precedents, Xiuyuan decided on the spot from what he had memorized, never hesitating in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then revising many institutions; whenever old precedents were needed, Xiuyuan answered from memory on the spot, never at a loss.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎任昉常謂之爲「孔獨誦」。

translations.literal: Personnel Section Director Ren Fang often called him "Kong Who Recites Alone."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang of the Personnel Section nicknamed him "Kong the Sole Reciter."

sentences.zh: 遷建康獄正，及辨訟折獄，時罕冤人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Corrector of Jiankang Prison; in judging lawsuits and deciding cases, rarely was anyone wrongly convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Corrector of Jiankang Prison, he heard cases with such care that wrongful convictions were rare.

sentences.zh: 後有選人爲獄司者，高祖尚引休源以勵之。

translations.literal: Later when someone was chosen for prison duty, the Emperor still cited Xiuyuan as an example to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: When a successor was later chosen for the prison post, Gaozu still held Xiuyuan up as the model.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人，司徒臨川王府記室參軍，遷尚書左丞，彈肅禮闈，雅允朝望。

translations.literal: Appointed Palace Secretary, Secretary to Prince of Linchuan's household, promoted to Left Assistant Director in the Masters of Writing—in the Rites Gate he was stern and upright, fully meeting the court's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Secretary and secretary to Prince of Linchuan, then Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, where his stern integrity in the examination hall won wide respect.

sentences.zh: 時太子詹事周舍撰《禮疑義》，自漢魏至于齊梁，並皆搜采，休源所有奏議，咸預編錄。

translations.literal: At that time the Crown Prince's Steward Zhou She compiled "Doubts on Rites," searching materials from Han and Wei through Qi and Liang; Xiuyuan's memorials and deliberations were all included in the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince's Steward Zhou She compiled Doubts on Rites, drawing on Han, Wei, Qi, and Liang, every memorial and opinion Xiuyuan had written was included.

sentences.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎，遷長兼御史中丞，正色直繩，無所回避，百僚莫不憚之。

translations.literal: Appointed Supervising Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate, promoted to Senior Concurrent Supervisor of Censors—in upright color and straight measure he deferred to nothing; all officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Made Supervising Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then Senior Concurrent Censor, he was unflinching in enforcing the law, and the whole bureaucracy feared him.

sentences.zh: 除少府卿，又兼行丹陽尹事。

translations.literal: Appointed Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury, additionally acting as Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Director of the Treasury and also acted as magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 出爲宣惠晉安王府長史、南郡太守、行荊州府州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief of the Princely Household of Propagation and Grace Prince of Jin'an, Administrator of Nan commandery, directing Jing province military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as chief secretary to Propagation and Grace Prince of Jin'an, administrator of Nan commandery, with charge of Jingzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂之曰：「荊州總上流沖要，義高分陝，今以十歲兒委卿，善匡翼之，勿憚周昌之舉也。

translations.literal: The Emperor told him: "Jing province is overall the upper reaches' strategic key; its meaning equals the high divide at Fen. Now I entrust to you a ten-year-old child—well guide and support him; do not shrink from a Zhou Chang's action.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told him: "Jingzhou guards the upper Yangzi and is as vital as the western frontier. I am placing a ten-year-old prince in your hands—guide him well, and do not hesitate to speak bluntly as Zhou Chang did.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣以庸鄙，曲荷恩遇，方揣丹誠，效其一割。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant, coarse and lowly, has curiously received your grace; I shall gauge my utmost sincerity and offer what little I can.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "I am a humble man who has received extraordinary favor; I will give whatever sincerity and effort I possess.

sentences.zh: 」上善其對，乃敕晉安王曰：「孔休源人倫儀錶，汝年尚幼，當每事師之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his reply and issued an edict to Prince of Jin'an: "Kong Xiuyuan is a model of human relations and deportment. You are still young—take him as teacher in every matter.
translations.idiomatic: " Pleased with the answer, Gaozu ordered Prince of Jin'an: "Kong Xiuyuan is a paragon of conduct. You are still young—let him be your teacher in all things.

sentences.zh: 」尋而始興王嶦代鎮荊州，復爲憺府長史，南郡太守、行府州事如故。

translations.literal: " Soon Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan replaced him as Jing governor; again he served as Chief of Dan's household, with Nan commandery administrator and directing military and civil affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: " When Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan took over Jingzhou, Xiuyuan stayed on as his chief secretary and Nan commandery administrator with the same duties as before.

sentences.zh: 在州累政，甚有治績，平心決斷，請託不行。

translations.literal: Through several terms in the province he had very good administrative achievements—deciding cases with an even hand, petitions and entreaties gaining no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Over several tours of duty he governed with real success, judging fairly and refusing every private request.

sentences.zh: 高祖深嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised him warmly for it.

sentences.zh: 除通直散騎常侍，領羽林監，轉秘書監，遷明威將軍，復爲晉安王府長史、南蘭陵太守，別敕專行南徐州事。

translations.literal: Appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, overseeing the Feathered Forest Guard, transferred to Director of the Secretariat, promoted to Bright Might General, again Chief of Jin'an's household and Administrator of South Lanling—separate edict put him solely in charge of South Xu affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and head of the Feathered Forest Guard, then Director of the Secretariat and Bright Might General, again chief secretary to Prince of Jin'an and administrator of South Lanling, with a special commission for South Xu alone.

sentences.zh: 休源累佐名籓，甚得民譽，王深相倚仗，軍民機務，動止詢謀。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan had repeatedly assisted famous fiefs, winning great popular repute; the prince deeply relied on him—military and civilian urgent business, every move and halt consulted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Having served several great princely domains, he enjoyed wide public esteem; the prince leaned on him heavily, consulting him on every military and civil decision.

sentences.zh: 常於中齋別施一榻，云「此是孔長史坐」，人莫得預焉。

translations.literal: He often set aside a separate couch in the central study, saying "This is Chief Kong's seat"—no one else might use it.
translations.idiomatic: In the inner study he kept a couch set apart, saying, "This seat is for Chief Secretary Kong," and no one else was allowed to sit there.

sentences.zh: 其見敬如此。

translations.literal: Such was the respect shown him.
translations.idiomatic: That was the measure of the honor he received.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子薨，有敕夜召休源入宴居殿，與羣公參定謀議，立晉安王綱爲皇太子。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, an edict summoned Xiuyuan at night to the dwelling hall for deliberation with the assembled lords on establishing Prince of Jin'an Gang as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Zhaoming's death, an edict called Xiuyuan to the palace at night to join the assembled ministers in choosing Prince of Jin'an Gang as heir.

sentences.zh: 四年，遘疾，高祖遣中使候問，並給醫藥，日有十數。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he fell ill; the Emperor sent palace envoys to inquire and provided medicine—ten or more each day.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he fell ill; Gaozu sent palace messengers to inquire after him and sent medicine ten or more times a day.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of that year, at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，節朔薦蔬菲而已。

translations.literal: His final instructions: simple burial, only vegetables at the seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He left orders for a plain funeral and only modest vegetable offerings at the seasonal rites.

sentences.zh: 高祖爲之流涕，顧謂謝舉曰：「孔休源奉職清忠，當官正直，方欲共康治道，以隆王化。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept for him and, turning to Xie Ju, said: "Kong Xiuyuan served his office with pure loyalty, upright as an official; I had hoped to jointly bring about good government and elevate kingly transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wept and, turning to Xie Ju, said: "Kong Xiuyuan served with pure loyalty and upright integrity. I had hoped to build good government with him and elevate the kingly way.

sentences.zh: 奄至殞歿，朕甚痛之。

translations.literal: Suddenly he is cut off—I grieve deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he is gone, and I grieve deeply."

sentences.zh: 」舉曰：「此人清介強直，當今罕有，微臣竊爲陛下惜之。

translations.literal: Ju said: "This man was pure and upright, strong and straight—rare today; your humble servant privately mourns him for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Ju replied: "He was incorruptible and resolute—a man rarely seen today. Your servant grieves for Your Majesty's loss."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「慎終追遠，歷代通規；

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed: "Care in death and remembrance of the distant—the common rule of all dynasties;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "To honor the dead and remember the distant is the custom of every age;

sentences.zh: 褒德疇庸，先王令典。

translations.literal: honoring virtue and rewarding merit—the worthy precedent of ancient kings.
translations.idiomatic: to praise virtue and reward service is the ancient kings' true law.

sentences.zh: 宣惠將軍、金紫光祿大夫、監揚州孔休源，風業貞正，雅量沖邈，升榮建禮，譽重搢紳。

translations.literal: Propagation and Grace General, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Supervisor of Yangzhou Kong Xiuyuan—his conduct and learning were upright and true, his generous measure serene and far-reaching; rising in honor at the Hall of Establishing Rites, his reputation weighed heavy among the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Propagation and Grace General, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Supervisor of Yangzhou Kong Xiuyuan was upright in character, broad in spirit, honored at the Hall of Establishing Rites, and esteemed among officials.

sentences.zh: 理務神州，化覃歌詠，方興仁壽，穆是髂倫。

translations.literal: He managed affairs in the heartland; his transforming influence spread to songs of praise; he was just raising benevolent longevity and harmonizing the moral order.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the central realm, won the people's praise in song, and was on the verge of bringing humane rule and moral order to fruition.

sentences.zh: 奄然永逝，倍用悲惻。

translations.literal: Suddenly he passed forever—doubly we use grief and sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is gone forever, and our sorrow is doubled.

sentences.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，賻第一材一具，布五十匹，錢五萬，蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; funeral gifts of one first-grade coffin set, fifty bolts of cloth, fifty thousand cash, and two hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with one first-grade coffin, fifty bolts of cloth, fifty thousand cash, and two hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 剋日舉哀。

translations.literal: Mourning shall be observed on the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites shall be held on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 喪事所須，隨由資給。

translations.literal: Whatever the funeral requires shall be supplied as needed.
translations.idiomatic: All funeral expenses shall be provided as required.

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Viscount of Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Viscount Zhen.

sentences.zh: 」皇太子手令曰：「金紫光祿大夫孔休源，立身中正，行己清恪。

translations.literal: The crown prince's handwritten order said: "Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Kong Xiuyuan stood upright in person and conducted himself with pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wrote: "Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Kong Xiuyuan was upright in bearing and pure in conduct.

sentences.zh: 昔歲西浮渚宮，東泊枌壤，毘佐蕃政，實盡厥誠。

translations.literal: In past years he served west at Zhugong Palace and east on the Fen frontier, assisting in princely governance with full sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years he served princes west at Zhugong and east on the Fen borderlands, giving his whole loyalty to their rule.

sentences.zh: 安國之詳審，公儀之廉白，無以過之。

translations.literal: The careful steadiness of one who steadies a state, the clean whiteness of one who balances the scales—none surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: His careful judgment in governing a realm and his spotless integrity surpass all comparison.

sentences.zh: 奄至殞喪，情用惻怛。

translations.literal: Suddenly he is cut off in death—my feelings are deeply pained.
translations.idiomatic: His sudden death fills me with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 今須舉哀，外可備禮。」

translations.literal: Now mourning must be observed; outwardly let the full rites be prepared."
translations.idiomatic: Mourning must now be observed; let the proper ceremonies be arranged."

sentences.zh: 休源少孤，立志操，風範強正，明練治體。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan was orphaned young but established resolve and character—strong and upright in bearing, clear and practiced in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Xiuyuan set his will and bearing early—resolute in character, clear in the ways of government.

sentences.zh: 持身儉約，學窮文藝，當官理務，不憚強禦，常以天下爲己任。

translations.literal: He lived frugally, mastered literary arts, handled official duties without fearing the powerful, and always took the realm as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal in private life, deeply learned in letters, fearless before the mighty in office, he always acted as though the empire rested on his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 高祖深委仗之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu relied on him completely.

sentences.zh: 累居顯職，纖毫無犯。

translations.literal: Through successive high posts not the slightest offense was found.
translations.idiomatic: Through one high appointment after another, he never committed the slightest fault.

sentences.zh: 性慎密，寡嗜好。

translations.literal: His nature was cautious and reserved, with few indulgences.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious by nature and had few appetites.

sentences.zh: 出入帷幄，未嘗言禁中事，世以此重之。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the inner councils he never spoke of palace secrets—and the world for this held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: In and out of the inner councils he never breathed a word of palace affairs, and for that the world respected him.

sentences.zh: 聚書盈七千卷，手自校治，凡奏議彈文，勒成十五卷。

translations.literal: He amassed more than seven thousand volumes of books and personally collated them; memorials and impeachments were compiled into fifteen fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He collected more than seven thousand books and collated them himself; his memorials and impeachments were gathered into fifteen fascicles.

sentences.zh: 長子雲童，頗有父風，而篤信佛理，遍持經戒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuntong showed much of his father's character but devoted himself to Buddhist principle, keeping the precepts throughout.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuntong inherited much of his father's manner but devoted himself to Buddhism and kept every precept.

sentences.zh: 官至岳陽王府諮議、東揚州別駕。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of Adviser to Prince of Yueyang's household and Deputy Governor of East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to adviser in Prince of Yueyang's household and deputy governor of East Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少子宗軌，聰敏有識度，歷尚書都官郎，司徒左西掾，中書郎。

translations.literal: His youngest son Zonggui was clever and perceptive, serving as Director in the Masters of Writing's Bureau of Punishments, Left Western Aide to the Minister of Works, and Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Zonggui was bright and discerning, and served as Director in the Bureau of Punishments, left western aide to the Minister of Works, and Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 江革，字休映，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖齊之，宋尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qizhi was Gold Section Director in the Song Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qizhi had been Gold Section Director under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父柔之，齊尚書倉部郎，有孝行，以母憂毀卒。

translations.literal: His father Rouzhi was Granaries Section Director under Qi, famed for filial conduct—he died from grief in mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rouzhi, Granaries Section Director under Qi, was renowned for filial piety and died of grief while mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 革幼而聰敏，早有才思，六歲便解屬文。

translations.literal: Ge was clever and sharp from childhood with early literary talent; at six he could already compose linked prose.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood and precocious in letters, Ge could write linked prose at six.

sentences.zh: 柔之深加賞器，曰：「此兒必興吾門。

translations.literal: Rouzhi prized him greatly and said: "This boy will raise our clan.
translations.idiomatic: Rouzhi admired him deeply and said, "This child will bring honor to our house.

sentences.zh: 」九歲丁父艱，與弟觀同生孤貧，傍無師友，兄弟自相訓勖，讀書精力不倦。

translations.literal: " At nine he entered mourning for his father; he and his younger brother Guan were together orphaned and poor, without teachers or friends nearby—the brothers urged each other on, reading with tireless energy.
translations.idiomatic: " At nine his father died. He and his younger brother Guan were left alone and poor, with no teachers near at hand; the two brothers pushed each other to study without rest.

sentences.zh: 十六喪母，以孝聞。

translations.literal: At sixteen he lost his mother and became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he lost his mother and became known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 服闋，與觀俱詣太學，補國子生，舉高第。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he and Guan both went to the Imperial Academy, enrolled as a student of the National University, and were selected at the top of the class.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he and Guan entered the Imperial Academy as National University students and graduated at the top of their class.

sentences.zh: 齊中書郎王融、吏部謝朓雅相欽重。

translations.literal: Qi Palace Secretary Wang Rong and Personnel Director Xie Tiao both held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, Palace Secretary of Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of Personnel, both admired him.

sentences.zh: 朓嘗宿衛，還過候革，時大雪，見革弊絮單席，而耽學不倦，嗟歎久之，乃脫所著襦，並手割半氈與革充臥具而去。

translations.literal: Tiao once returned from palace guard duty and visited Ge; it was snowing heavily—seeing Ge in worn cotton with only a thin mat yet studying without tiring, Tiao sighed for a long time, took off the padded jacket he wore, and with his own hands cut half a felt mat for Ge's bedding before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Once, coming off palace guard duty in heavy snow, Tiao visited Ge and found him in patched cotton on a thin mat, still studying without pause. Tiao sighed long, gave him the padded jacket he was wearing, and cut half his felt mat by hand for Ge's bedding before he left.

sentences.zh: 司徒竟陵王聞其名，引爲西邸學士。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Jingling heard his fame and brought him in as a Western Pavilion scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingling, Minister of Works, heard of him and made him a Western Pavilion scholar.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉南徐州秀才。

translations.literal: At weak-cap age he was selected as xiucai of South Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was chosen xiucai of South Xu province.

sentences.zh: 時豫章胡諧之行州事，王融與諧之書，令薦革。

translations.literal: At that time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting provincial governor; Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was then acting governor; Wang Rong wrote urging him to recommend Ge.

sentences.zh: 諧之方貢琅邪王泛，便以革代之。

translations.literal: Xiezhi was about to present Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and substituted Ge in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi had intended to send up Wang Fan of Langya as the provincial tribute candidate and replaced him with Ge.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: Upon first office he became Court Gentleman for Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was Court Gentleman for Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 僕射江祏深相引接，祏爲太子詹事，啓革爲府丞。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Jiang Shi deeply drew him close; when Shi became Crown Prince's Steward he memorialized for Ge as household aide.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Jiang Shi took a strong liking to him; when Shi became Crown Prince's Steward he recommended Ge as household aide.

sentences.zh: 祏時權傾朝右，以革才堪經國，令參掌機務，詔誥文檄，皆委以具。

translations.literal: At the time Shi's power bent the court to the right; seeing Ge's talent fit for statecraft, he had him participate in urgent affairs—edicts and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.
translations.idiomatic: Shi then dominated the court; judging Ge capable of statecraft, he put him in charge of urgent business, and all edicts and dispatches were drafted by Ge.

sentences.zh: 革防杜形跡，外人不知。

translations.literal: Ge guarded against revealing traces—outsiders did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Ge kept his role hidden, and outsiders never knew.

sentences.zh: 祏誅，賓客皆罹其罪，革獨以智免。

translations.literal: When Shi was executed, his guests all suffered in his crime; Ge alone escaped through wit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi was executed, every man in his circle was implicated; Ge alone escaped through cleverness.

sentences.zh: 除尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: Appointed Driving Section Director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Driving Section Director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，高祖入石頭，時吳興太守袁昂據郡距義師，乃使革制書與昂，于坐立成，辭義典雅，高祖深賞歎之，因令與徐勉同掌書記。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing the Emperor entered Stone Fort; at that time Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery against the righteous army—Ge was sent to compose the imperial letter to Ang and finished it standing at the desk; its phrasing was elegant and classical, and the Emperor deeply admired it, then had him jointly manage written records with Xu Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongxing year 1 Gaozu entered Stone Fort while Yuan Ang, administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery against the cause. Ge was told to draft the letter to Ang and finished it on the spot; its language was elegant, Gaozu praised it highly, and put him in charge of written records together with Xu Mian.

sentences.zh: 建安王爲雍州刺史，表求管記，以革爲征北記室參軍，帶中廬令。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an was made Inspector of Yong province and requested a chief secretary; Ge was made Secretary to the Northern Expedition, concurrently Commander of the Central Banners.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jian'an became inspector of Yongzhou and asked for a chief secretary, Ge was made secretary to the northern expedition staff and concurrently commander of the central banners.

sentences.zh: 與弟觀少長共居，不忍離別，苦求同行，乃以觀爲征北行參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: He and his brother Guan had lived together from youth and could not bear to part; Guan begged hard to go together, so Guan was made Acting Secretary to the Northern Expedition, additionally secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He and Guan had lived together since childhood and could not bear to separate; Guan pleaded to go with him, and was made acting secretary on the northern expedition staff, additionally serving as secretary.

sentences.zh: 時吳興沈約、樂安任昉，並相賞重，昉與革書云：「此段雍府妙選英才，文房之職，總卿昆季，可謂馭二龍於長途，騁騏驥於千里。

translations.literal: At the time Shen Yue of Wuxing and Ren Fang of Le'an both prized him; Fang wrote to Ge: "This segment of the Yong prefecture household is a fine selection of talent—the literary office, both you brothers hold it—one may say driving two dragons on a long road, galloping fine steeds a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue of Wuxing and Ren Fang of Le'an both valued him. Fang wrote to Ge: "The Yongzhou staff has chosen its finest men—you and your brother both hold the literary office. It is like driving two dragons on a long road or running twin thoroughbreds a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 」途次江夏，觀遇疾卒。

translations.literal: " En route at Jiangxia, Guan fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: " On the road at Jiangxia, Guan fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 革時在雍，爲府王所禮，款若布衣。

translations.literal: Ge was then in Yong, treated by the prince with the warmth of a commoner's friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was then in Yongzhou, and the prince treated him with the easy warmth of an old friend.

sentences.zh: 王被徵爲丹陽尹，以革爲記室，領五官掾，除通直散騎常侍，建康正。

translations.literal: The prince was summoned as Magistrate of Danyang; Ge was made secretary, overseeing the Five Officials Aide, appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Chief of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was recalled as magistrate of Danyang, Ge became his secretary, head of the Five Officials section, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and chief of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 頻遷秣陵、建康令。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Magistrate of Moling and Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to magistrate of Moling and Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 爲治明肅，豪強憚之。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and stern—the powerful feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with clarity and severity, and the local strongmen feared him.

sentences.zh: 入爲中書舍人，尚書左丞，司農卿，復出爲雲麾晉安王長史、尋陽太守、行江州府事。

translations.literal: He entered as Palace Writer Attendant, Left Assistant Director of the Ministry of Works, and Minister of Agriculture; then went out again as Chief Clerk to Prince Jin'an of Cloud Banner, Administrator of Xunyang, and overseer of Jiangzhou prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Palace Writer Attendant, Left Assistant Director of the Ministry of Works, and Minister of Agriculture, then went out again as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an of Cloud Banner, administrator of Xunyang, and acting head of Jiangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 徙仁威廬陵王長史，太守、行事如故，以清嚴爲百城所憚。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Chief Clerk to Prince Renwei of Luling; his posts as administrator and acting deputy remained unchanged, and every commandery feared him for his probity and severity.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to chief clerk for Prince Renwei of Luling, he kept the same administrator and acting duties, and commanderies across the realm feared his austerity.

sentences.zh: 時少王行事多傾意于簽帥，革以正直自居，不與簽帥等同坐。

translations.literal: At the time young princes' acting deputies often deferred to their chiefs of staff; Ge held himself to rectitude and would not sit with chiefs of staff as equals.
translations.idiomatic: Young princes' acting deputies usually bowed to their chiefs of staff; Ge stood on principle and refused to share a seat with them.

sentences.zh: 俄遷左光祿大夫、南平王長史、御史中丞，彈奏豪權，一無所避。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Grand Master of Lustrous Virtue, Chief Clerk to Prince Nanping, and Censor-in-Chief, impeaching powerful magnates without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose to Left Grand Master of Lustrous Virtue, chief clerk to Prince Nanping, and censor-in-chief, impeaching the mighty without flinching.

sentences.zh: 除少府卿，出爲貞威將軍、北中郎南康王長史、廣陵太守，改授鎮北豫章王長史，將軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, went out as General of Loyal Might, Chief Clerk to Prince Nankang of North Central Command and Administrator of Guangling, then reassigned as Chief Clerk to Prince Zhenbei of Yuzhang; his generalship and administrator's post were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, he went out as General of Loyal Might, chief clerk to Prince Nankang of North Central Command and administrator of Guangling, then was reassigned chief clerk to Prince Zhenbei of Yuzhang while keeping the same generalship and magistracy.

sentences.zh: 時魏徐州刺史元法僧降附，革被敕隨府王鎮彭城。

translations.literal: When Wei Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng surrendered and submitted, Ge was ordered to follow the princely household to garrison Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng, Wei governor of Xuzhou, surrendered, Ge was ordered to follow the prince and garrison Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 城旣失守，革素不便馬，乃泛舟而還，途經下邳，遂爲魏人所執。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Ge had never been comfortable on horseback; he took boat instead, and passing through Xiapi was seized by Wei men.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. Ge had never ridden well; he took to the river instead, and at Xiapi Wei soldiers seized him.

sentences.zh: 魏徐州刺史元延明聞革才名，厚加接待。

translations.literal: Wei Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Yanming, hearing of Ge's literary reputation, treated him with great honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yanming, Wei governor of Xuzhou, had heard of Ge's fame and received him with deep respect.

sentences.zh: 革稱患腳不拜，延明將加害焉，見革辭色嚴正，更相敬重。

translations.literal: Ge pleaded a lame leg and would not bow; Yanming was about to harm him, but seeing Ge's stern dignity in speech and bearing, treated him with renewed respect.
translations.idiomatic: Ge claimed a bad leg and refused to bow. Yanming meant to punish him, but Ge's stern bearing in word and face won respect instead.

sentences.zh: 時祖𣈶同被拘執，延明使𣈶作《欹器》、《漏刻銘》，革罵𣈶曰：「卿荷國厚恩，已無報答，今乃爲虜立銘，孤負朝廷。

translations.literal: At the time Zu Can was also detained; Yanming had Can compose inscriptions for the Tilting Vessel and the Clepsydra. Ge cursed Can: "You received the state's deep grace yet have no repayment; now you write inscriptions for the enemy—betraying the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Can was held with him. Yanming had Can write inscriptions for the Tilting Vessel and the Clepsydra. Ge reviled him: "The state heaped grace on you and you never repaid it. Now you write for the captors and betray the court.

sentences.zh: 」延明聞之，乃令革作丈八寺碑並祭彭祖文，革辭以囚執旣久，無復心思。

translations.literal: " Yanming heard and ordered Ge to write the Zhangba Temple stele and a text sacrificing to Peng Zu; Ge refused, saying long captivity had left him no heart for such work.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanming then ordered Ge to compose the Zhangba Temple stele and a sacrifice to Peng Zu. Ge refused: long imprisonment had drained his mind.

sentences.zh: 延明逼之逾苦，將加箠撲。

translations.literal: Yanming pressed him harder and would have had him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming pressed harder and was about to have him flogged.

sentences.zh: 革厲色而言曰：「江革行年六十，不能殺身報主，今日得死爲幸，誓不爲人執筆。

translations.literal: Ge said with stern countenance: "Jiang Ge is sixty years old; unable to give his life for his lord, today to die would be fortune—I swear never to write at another's command.
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, face hard: "Jiang Ge is sixty. I could not die for my lord; to die today would be luck. I swear I will never take up the brush for another man.

sentences.zh: 」延明知不可屈，乃止。

translations.literal: " Yanming knew he could not be broken and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanming saw he could not be bent and desisted.

sentences.zh: 日給脫粟三升，僅餘性命。

translations.literal: Each day they gave him three sheng of husked millet—barely enough to keep life.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he received three sheng of husked millet—just enough to stay alive.

sentences.zh: 值魏主討中山王元略反北，乃放革及祖𣈶還朝。

translations.literal: It happened the Wei ruler marched north to suppress Prince Zhongshan Yuan Lue's rebellion; Ge and Zu Can were released and sent back to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei ruler marched north against Prince Zhongshan Yuan Lue's rebellion, Ge and Zu Can were freed and sent home to court.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「前貞威將軍、鎮北長史、廣陵太守江革，才思通贍，出內有聞，在朝正色，臨危不撓，首佐台鉉，實允僉諧。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Former General of Loyal Might, Chief Clerk of Zhenbei, and Administrator of Guangling Jiang Ge—talented in thought and expression, known inside and outside court, upright in office, unmoved in peril, chief aide to the Three Dukes—all agreed he was fit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "Jiang Ge, former General of Loyal Might, chief clerk of Zhenbei, and administrator of Guangling—gifted in mind and word, known in court and out, upright in office, unbroken in danger, chief aide to the Three Dukes—fully worthy of trust.

sentences.zh: 可太尉臨川王長史。」

translations.literal: Appoint him Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal, Prince Linchuan."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be chief clerk to the Grand Marshal, Prince Linchuan."

sentences.zh: 時高祖盛於佛教，朝賢多啓求受戒，革精信因果，而高祖未知，謂革不奉佛教，乃賜革《覺意詩》五百字，云「惟當勤精進，自強行勝脩；

translations.literal: Gaozu was then zealous for Buddhism; court worthies often petitioned to receive ordination. Ge faithfully believed in karma, but Gaozu did not know and thought Ge did not embrace Buddhism; he bestowed on Ge a five-hundred-character "Awakened Intent Poem," saying "Only diligent effort and self-strengthening surpass cultivation;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then deep in Buddhism; court worthies often asked to take vows. Ge truly believed in karma, but Gaozu did not know and thought he rejected the faith. He gave Ge a five-hundred-character "Awakened Intent Poem," saying, "Only diligence and self-strengthening beat empty practice;

sentences.zh: 豈可作底突，如彼必死囚。

translations.literal: How can one be a stubborn bump, like those condemned prisoners?
translations.idiomatic: Who would be a stubborn bump, like a man already condemned to die?

sentences.zh: 以此告江革，並及諸貴遊。

translations.literal: Let this be told to Jiang Ge, and also to the other noble travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Tell this to Jiang Ge, and to the other noble travelers as well.

sentences.zh: 」又手敕云：「世間果報，不可不信，豈得底突如對元延明邪？

translations.literal: " Also a handwritten edict: "Worldly retribution cannot be disbelieved—how can one be a stubborn bump as before Yuan Yanming?
translations.idiomatic: " A handwritten edict added: "Worldly retribution is real. How can you be a stubborn bump with Yuan Yanming as you were before?

sentences.zh: 」革因啓乞受菩薩戒。

translations.literal: " Ge thereupon memorialized requesting to receive the bodhisattva precepts.
translations.idiomatic: " Ge then memorialized asking to receive the bodhisattva precepts.

sentences.zh: 重除少府卿、長史、校尉。

translations.literal: Again appointed Minister of the Lesser Treasury, Chief Clerk, and Colonel Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Minister of the Lesser Treasury, chief clerk, and colonel commandant.

sentences.zh: 時武陵王在東州，頗自驕縱，上召革面敕曰：「武陵王年少，臧盾性弱，不能匡正，欲以卿代爲行事。

translations.literal: Prince Wuling was in East Yangzhou and rather arrogant and unrestrained; the Emperor summoned Ge and personally charged him: "Prince Wuling is young; Zang Dun is timid by nature and cannot correct him—I wish to have you replace him as acting administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuling held East Yangzhou and had grown proud and loose. The emperor summoned Ge and charged him in person: "Prince Wuling is young. Zang Dun is mild and cannot correct him. I want you to replace him as acting administrator.

sentences.zh: 非卿不可，不得有辭。

translations.literal: No one but you will do; you may not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: No one but you will do. You may not refuse.

sentences.zh: 」乃除折沖將軍、東中郎武陵王長史、會稽郡丞、行府州事。

translations.literal: " Appointed General Who Breaks the Charge, Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling of East Central Command, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji, overseeing prefectural and commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made General Who Breaks the Charge, chief clerk to Prince Wuling of East Central Command, assistant administrator of Kuaiji, and acting head of prefectural and commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 革門生故吏，家多在東州，聞革應至，並齎持緣道迎候。

translations.literal: Ge's former students and subordinates, many with homes in East Yangzhou, hearing Ge was coming, all brought gifts along the road to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Ge's former students and subordinates lived in East Yangzhou. Hearing he was coming, they lined the road with gifts to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 革曰：「我通不受餉，不容獨當故人筐篚。

translations.literal: Ge said: "I have never accepted gifts—I cannot alone take my old friends' baskets and boxes.
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "I never take gifts. I cannot be the only one to fill my old friends' baskets and boxes.

sentences.zh: 」至鎮，惟資公俸，食不兼味。

translations.literal: " On reaching his post he relied only on official salary; his meals had no second dish.
translations.idiomatic: " At his post he lived only on official salary and never ate more than one dish at a meal.

sentences.zh: 郡境殷廣，辭訟日數百，革分判辨析，曾無疑滯。

translations.literal: The commandery was vast and populous; lawsuits ran to hundreds per day—Ge divided and judged them, never once stalling in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was broad and crowded; lawsuits came by the hundred each day. Ge divided and decided them without a moment's hesitation.

sentences.zh: 功必賞，過必罰，民安吏畏，百城震恐。

translations.literal: Merit always rewarded, fault always punished; the people were at peace, officials feared him, and every city trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was always rewarded and fault always punished. The people rested easy, officials feared him, and every city shook.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王騫爲山陰令，贓貨狼藉，望風自解。

translations.literal: Wang Qian of Langye was magistrate of Shanyin—his bribery was flagrant; at Ge's approach he resigned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian of Langye, magistrate of Shanyin, was awash in bribes. At Ge's coming he resigned before the wind.

sentences.zh: 府王憚之，遂雅相欽重。

translations.literal: The princely household feared him and thereafter held him in deep esteem.
translations.idiomatic: The prince feared him and thereafter held him in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 每至侍宴，言論必以《詩》《書》，王因此耽學好文。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, his talk always drew on the Odes and Documents; the Prince therefore devoted himself to study and letters.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet his talk turned to the Odes and Documents, and the prince came to love learning and letters.

sentences.zh: 典簽沈熾文以王所制詩呈高祖，高祖謂僕射徐勉曰：「江革果能稱職。

translations.literal: Chief of Staff Shen Chiwen presented the Prince's poems to Gaozu; Gaozu said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Jiang Ge has indeed proved equal to his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Chief of staff Shen Chiwen showed the prince's poems to Gaozu. Gaozu told Vice Director Xu Mian, "Jiang Ge has truly done his duty.

sentences.zh: 」乃除都官尚書。

translations.literal: " Appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 將還，民皆戀惜之，贈遺無所受。

translations.literal: When he was about to leave, the people all cherished him and wished to keep him—he accepted no parting gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to leave, the people clung to him with grief. He took no parting gifts.

sentences.zh: 送故依舊訂舫，革並不納，惟乘臺所給一舸。

translations.literal: Escorts provisioned a boat as usual; Ge would none of it and took only the single craft the office provided.
translations.idiomatic: Escorts arranged a boat as always. Ge refused it and took only the single vessel the office gave him.

sentences.zh: 舸艚偏欹，不得安臥。

translations.literal: The boat listed to one side—he could not lie at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The boat listed to one side, and he could not lie down in comfort.

sentences.zh: 或謂革曰：「船旣不平，濟江甚險，當移徙重物，以迮輕艚。

translations.literal: Someone said to Ge: "The boat is unsteady—crossing the river will be perilous; you should shift heavy objects to ballast the lighter hull.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Ge, "The boat is unsteady. Crossing the river will be dangerous. Move heavy things to weigh down the lighter hull.

sentences.zh: 」革旣無物，乃於西陵岸取石十餘片以實之。

translations.literal: " Ge had nothing; he went to the West Mausoleum shore and took a dozen-odd stones to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: " Ge owned nothing. He went to the West Mausoleum shore, took more than ten stones, and loaded them aboard.

sentences.zh: 其清貧如此。

translations.literal: Such was his austerity and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his austerity.

sentences.zh: 尋監吳郡。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was put in charge of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 于時境內荒儉，劫盜公行。

translations.literal: At the time the territory was barren and hungry; robber bands operated openly.
translations.idiomatic: The land was then famine-stricken, and bandits roamed openly.

sentences.zh: 革至郡，惟有公給仗身二十人，百姓皆懼不能靜寇；

translations.literal: When Ge reached the commandery he had only twenty armed attendants from the office; the people all feared he could not quell bandits;
translations.idiomatic: When Ge arrived he had only twenty armed attendants from the office. The people feared he could not still the bandits;

sentences.zh: 反省游軍尉，民下逾恐。

translations.literal: hearing he intended to review the patrol commandant, the populace grew still more alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: and when they heard he meant to inspect the patrol commandant, fear only deepened.

sentences.zh: 革乃廣施恩撫，明行制令，盜賊靜息，民吏安之。

translations.literal: Ge then broadly dispensed kindness and encouragement, clearly enforced regulations—bandits quieted, people and officials were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Ge then showed broad kindness, enforced clear rules, and the bandits fell silent. People and officials alike were at peace.

sentences.zh: 武陵王出鎮江州，乃曰：「我得江革，文華清麗，豈能一日忘之，當與其同飽。

translations.literal: When Prince Wuling went out to garrison Jiangzhou he said: "I gained Jiang Ge—refined and elegant in letters—how could I forget him in a day? I shall share my meals with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wuling went out to garrison Jiangzhou he said, "I gained Jiang Ge—refined and bright in letters. How could I forget him in a day? I shall eat with him.

sentences.zh: 」乃表革同行。

translations.literal: " He memorialized for Ge to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized for Ge to go with him.

sentences.zh: 又除明威將軍、南中郎長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: Also appointed General of Bright Might, Chief Clerk of South Central Command, and Administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was also made General of Bright Might, chief clerk of South Central Command, and administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 徵入爲度支尚書。

translations.literal: Summoned as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 好獎進閭閻，爲後生延譽，由是衣冠士子，翕然歸之。

translations.literal: He loved to encourage village folk and build reputations for the young—therefore gentry and scholars flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to lift up common folk and speak well of the young, and gentry and scholars gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令何敬容掌選，序用多非其人。

translations.literal: Minister of Works He Jingrong controlled appointments; the ranked selections were often unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works He Jingrong controlled appointments, and many of his choices were unworthy.

sentences.zh: 革性強直，每至朝宴，恒有褒貶，以此爲權勢所疾，乃謝病還家。

translations.literal: Ge was by nature forceful and upright; at every court banquet he always had praise and blame—therefore the powerful hated him, and he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was forceful and upright. At every court banquet he praised and blamed without restraint. The powerful resented him, and he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 除光祿大夫、領步兵校尉、南、北兗二州大中正，優遊閑放，以文酒自娛。

translations.literal: Appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers, and Chief Arbiter of South and North Yan provinces—leisurely and at ease, he took pleasure in letters and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, colonel of footsoldiers, and chief arbiter of South and North Yan provinces, and lived at ease with letters and wine.

sentences.zh: 大同元年二月，卒，諡曰強子。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Datong he died; posthumous title Qiangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Datong he died. His posthumous title was Qiangzi.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works in twenty scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, twenty scrolls, circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 革歷官八府長史，四王行事，三爲二千石，傍無姬侍，家徒壁立，世以此高之。

translations.literal: Ge served as chief clerk in eight princely households, acted for four princes, thrice held two-thousand-household posts, had no concubines at his side, and his home stood bare as walls—the world honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Ge had been chief clerk in eight princely households, acting deputy for four princes, and thrice held two-thousand-household posts. He kept no concubines, and his house stood bare as walls. The world honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 長子行敏，好學有才俊，官至通直郎，早卒，有集五卷。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingmin loved learning and had talent; he reached Direct Communication Gentleman, died young, and left collected works in five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xingmin loved learning and had talent. He reached Direct Communication Gentleman, died young, and left five scrolls of collected works.

sentences.zh: 次子從簡，少有文情，年十七，作《采荷詞》以刺敬容，爲當時所賞。

translations.literal: Second son Congjian had literary sensibility from youth; at seventeen he wrote "Song of Gathering Lotus" to satirize Jingrong and won acclaim in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Congjian had literary feeling from youth. At seventeen he wrote "Song of Gathering Lotus" to satirize Jingrong, and his age praised it.

sentences.zh: 歷官司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He served as aide to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，爲任約所害。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he was killed by Ren Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Ren Yue killed him.

sentences.zh: 子兼叩頭流血，乞代父命，以身蔽刃，遂俱見殺。

translations.literal: His son Jian kowtowed until blood flowed, begging to die in his father's place and shielding him with his body—they were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian kowtowed until blood ran, begging to die in his father's place and covering him with his body. Both were killed.

sentences.zh: 天下莫不痛之。

translations.literal: All under heaven grieved.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven grieved.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高祖留心政道，孔休源以識治見知，旣遇其時，斯爲幸矣。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Gaozu attended to governance; Kong Xiuyuan was recognized for his discernment in administration—having met his time, this was fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Gaozu cared for good government. Kong Xiuyuan was known for his grasp of rule, and to meet such a time was fortune.

sentences.zh: 江革聰敏亮直，亦一代之盛名歟。

translations.literal: Jiang Ge was quick-witted, brilliant, and upright—is he not a famed name of his generation?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ge was quick, bright, and upright—a famed name of his generation, surely.

translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.idiomatic: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
